record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.original_question: Let A be a non-diagonalizable n × n matrix whose entries are nonnegative algebraic numbers, and regard A as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph G. Fix an algebraic number β ≠ 0. If two vertices i and j satisfy [e^{βA}]_{ii} = [e^{βA}]_{jj}, must i and j be cospectral, meaning that [A^r]_{ii} = [A^r]_{jj} for every integer r ≥ 0? Prove this statement or provide a counterexample.

evidence.quote: Definition 2.2. Two vertices i, j of G are cospectral if for every integer r ≥ 0, [Ar]ii = [Ar]jj .

Problem 1. Let A be a (non diagonalizable) n × n matrix, whose entries are all nonnegative algebraic numbers, regarded as the adjacency matrix of a weighted directed graph G. Let β ̸= 0 be an algebraic number. Prove or disprove the following statement: if for two vertices i, j we have [eβA]ii = [eβA]jj , then i and j are cospectral.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix whose entries are nonnegative algebraic numbers, and assume that $A$ is not diagonalizable over $\mathbb{C}$. Regard $A$ as the (weighted) adjacency matrix of a directed graph $G$ on vertex set $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$, where the entry $A_{ij}$ is the weight of the arc from $i$ to $j$. Two vertices $i$ and $j$ of $G$ are called cospectral if $[A^r]_{ii} = [A^r]_{jj}$ for every integer $r \geq 0$. Define, for any complex number $\beta$, the matrix exponential $e^{\beta A} = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(\beta A)^k}{k!}$.

Fix a nonzero algebraic number $\beta$. Prove or disprove: if two vertices $i$ and $j$ satisfy
$$[e^{\beta A}]_{ii} = [e^{\beta A}]_{jj},$$
then $i$ and $j$ are cospectral.
artifact.category_tag: spectral graph theory and subgraph centrality
artifact.status_search_result: Existing results (Kloster–Král–Sullivan and follow-up work proving Estrada's conjecture and generalizations) establish that equal $\beta$-subgraph centrality implies cospectrality when the adjacency matrix is diagonalizable (including weighted undirected graphs and digraphs with real spectrum and diagonalizable $A$). The non-diagonalizable case with algebraic nonnegative entries is explicitly noted as not covered by these methods, and no published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Vertex distinction with subgraph centrality: A proof of Estrada's conjecture and some generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: For algebraic β, two vertices with equal β-subgraph centrality are necessarily cospectral, settling Estrada's conjecture and a generalization due to Kloster, Král and Sullivan; results apply to weighted undirected graphs and to digraphs with real spectrum and diagonalizable adjacency matrix.
status_evidence.claim: The cospectrality conclusion has been proved under a diagonalizability hypothesis, leaving the non-diagonalizable case unresolved.

status_evidence.title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality (ResearchGate listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems related to subgraph centrality, including cases beyond the diagonalizable setting.
status_evidence.claim: The non-diagonalizable algebraic case is posed as an open problem.
